en: Conditioned by a state that is non-visible, non-reacting, and non-conflictual, there arises a state that is non-visible, non-reacting, and conflictual, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Three under root; ... pe ... three under non-disappearance.
In dependence on a state that is non-visible, non-reacting, and non-conflictual, there arises a state that is visible, reacting, and non-conflictual, by way of root condition; ... seven.
In dependence on a state that is non-visible, non-reacting, and non-conflictual, there arises a state that is visible, reacting, and non-conflictual, by way of root condition; ... seven.

Dependent on a state that is non-visible, non-reacting, and non-afflictive, and [dependent on] a state that is non-visible, non-reacting, and non-afflictive, a state that is visible, reacting, and non-afflictive arises by way of root condition... seven. (Abbreviated.
Under root, twenty-one; under predominance, twenty-one ... pe ... under non-disappearance, twenty-one.
(The "Conascent Chapter" should also be expanded in the same manner as the "Dependent Chapter.")

22.36.1. Root Condition with Respect to the Object and Other Factors A state that is non-visible, non-reacting, and non-obstructive (na-anidassana-appaṭigha-na-āraṇa) is a condition, by way of root-condition (hetu-paccaya), for a state that is visible, reacting, and obstructive (sanidassana-sappaṭigha-āraṇa). ...
[Seven] A state that is non-visible, non-reacting, and non-obstructive is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is visible, reacting, and obstructive. ... [Seven]

States that are non-visible, non-reacting, and non-conflictual, and states that are non-visible, non-reacting, and non-conflictual, are related to a state that is visible, reacting, and conflictual by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*)—seven [ways].

A state that is non-visible, non-reacting, and non-conflictual is related to a state that is non-visible, non-reacting, and non-conflictual by way of the object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*). A state that is non-visible, non-reacting, and non-conflictual is related to a state that is non-visible, non-reacting...
A non-conflictual state is a condition for [another] non-conflictual state by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*).
Non-indemonstrable-and-non-reactive and non-conflictual states are conditions for a non-indemonstrable-and-non-reactive non-conflictual state by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root condition, twenty-one; in object condition, three; in predominance condition, twenty-one; in proximity condition, three ... pe ...
in conascence, dependence, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, path, dissociation conditions, twenty-one ...
(Just as the positive, the negative, the positive-negative, and the negative-positive were calculated for the section on questions in the *Kusalattika*, so too should they be calculated here.)
